problems.source_says: H1a-prime explicitly contrasts similarity to the author's own writing with similarity to different participants' writing; Table 8 also varies same versus different reference author. This meets the codebook definition of diversity, which includes similarity across different people's outputs. The form's rationale that this is not an arm-level diversity score adds a restriction absent from the codebook. Code diversity rather than other; this is not within-person flexibility.
problems.quote: Post-editing will make participants’ AI-assisted writing sound more like their own unassisted writing than it does like other participants’ unassisted writing.
problems.locator: PDF p. 3, section 3, H1a-prime; p. 6, section 6.1 and Figure 5 left; p. 21, Table 8; creativity-codebook.md section 6, Construct (lines 84-87).

problems.source_says: The scored post-edited output was produced using the supplied AI draft. Once H1a-prime is classified as diversity because it compares different writers, the codebook requires across_people. Its comparison to an unassisted reference does not turn the scored treatment output into an after_ai outcome.
problems.quote: An outcome produced with AI available is `across_people` when its construct is diversity and `with_ai` otherwise.
problems.locator: creativity-codebook.md section 1 (line 17); PDF pp. 4-5, Figure 2 and section 4; p. 6, Figure 5 left.

problems.source_says: The PDF identifies which reference texts are compared, but does not explicitly establish whether the main H2c, H1a-prime, H1b, and H1c tests use individual document-reference pairs or similarities aggregated within an output. Appendix A.2 specifies one own-control reference embedding from concatenated texts for H1a and task matching for LLM references; it does not supply the aggregation rule for these other tests. Figure 6 explicitly calls H2a/H2b pair comparisons, but that does not establish the observation unit for every other hypothesis. Under the codebook's definition of the paper's analysis unit, these four definite pair codes remain unsupported; the unresolved units should be null. This is a lack of confirmation, not proof that the actual units were different. The form acknowledges missing aggregation details but nevertheless assigns pair.
problems.quote: Where applicable, we match the writing tasks in reference texts between comparisons.
problems.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, sections 6-6.2 and Figures 3-5; p. 7, Figure 6; pp. 13-14, Appendix A.2; p. 19, Appendix B.5; p. 21, Table 8; creativity-codebook.md section 6, Unit (line 101).

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 establishes criterion 3: LUAR cosine similarities are computed between actual texts from different participants. Diversity, across_people, embedding_similarity, and pair are explicitly supported for H2a/H2b.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, section 5.2; p. 6, section 6.2; p. 7, Figure 6 caption.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 is an output-based comparison of other writers' post-edited text against own unassisted text, supporting diversity/across_people and embedding_similarity; it is a reference-source contrast, not a separate randomized assistance contrast.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, H2c; p. 6, section 6.2 and Figure 5 right.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 scores personal stylistic self-similarity using embeddings, supporting other/with_ai. Appendix A.2 describes a score for each treatment text against its author's concatenated control reference, supporting output; it does not count idea categories.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, sections 5.2 and 6.1; p. 13, Appendix A.2.

confirmed.statement: S1-O4 is computed on writing, not self-reported. The form correctly preserves the source ambiguity between the prose about stylistic shifts and Figure 5's final similarity levels.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, section 6.1 and Figure 5 left; p. 16, Table 3; p. 21, Table 8.

confirmed.statement: S1-O5 scores resemblance to LLM text using LUAR/CISR; Pangram separately estimates AI-authorship likelihood on an individual text. The form explicitly documents Pangram's automated method and output unit within the grouped H1b outcome; other/with_ai is appropriate for AI-likeness.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, sections 5.2 and 6.1; p. 16, Table 3, H1b; pp. 18-19, Table 5 and Appendix B.5.

confirmed.statement: S1-O6 compares the same post-edited output with own human and LLM references, supporting other/with_ai and embedding_similarity. Table 6's same-participant label is genuinely inconsistent with its reference-source caption, as the form notes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, section 6.1 and Figure 4 right; pp. 18-19, Table 6 and Appendix B.5.

confirmed.statement: S1-O7 is model-scored linguistic acceptability of each text, not a participant self-rating. Usefulness as narrow language quality, automated_score, output, and with_ai follow the codebook and measurement description.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 20, Figure 12; p. 21, Appendix B.7.1; creativity-codebook.md section 6.

confirmed.statement: For all seven outcomes the treatment writing was produced by editing a supplied LLM draft, supporting AI available=yes and immediate timing. The control block was separate unassisted writing; no distinct delayed or post-removal creativity test is reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, Figures 1-2 and section 4; p. 24, Appendix D and Table 9; p. 28, Figure 20 caption.

confirmed.statement: All 15 retained main p-value, Hedges' g, and confidence-interval tuples for H1a, H1a-prime, H1b, H1c, H2a, H2b, and H2c exactly match Table 3, including LUAR-MUD, CISR, and Pangram results.

All nine retained regression rows match the printed estimates, SEs, z statistics, p-values, and intervals in Tables 4-6 and 8. The form retains Table 8 separately from the main H1a-prime contrast and does not relabel Table 6's unresolved predictor.

The CoLA contrasts match the prose exactly: post-edited versus human control is reported as p < .0001, g = -1.29, CI [-1.57, -1.05]; post-edited versus original LLM text is p < .0001, g = 0.59, CI [0.45, 0.73]. The directional ranking and the form's warnings about printed signs are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 21, Appendix B.7.1; p. 20, Figure 12.

confirmed.statement: H1 and H2 are explicitly the two main preregistered hypotheses; CoLA is explicitly exploratory. The corresponding primary/secondary outcome labels are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, section 3; p. 21, Appendix B.7.1.

confirmed.statement: Self-perceived authenticity, willingness to use text, and originality-related preference rankings are self-reports and do not supply missing scored-output creativity outcomes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, section 6.3 and Figures 7-8; p. 17, Appendix B.3 and Figure 9; p. 19, Appendix B.6 and Table 7.

confirmed.statement: No additional qualifying creativity/diversity endpoint was found in the appendices: initial-generation consistency and authorship benchmarks validate the design/measure; lexical counts and edit-span characteristics describe editing. Associations with self-similarity concern the existing S1-O3 outcome.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 14-16, Appendices B.1-B.2 and Tables 1-3; pp. 17-18, Appendix B.4; pp. 21-22, Appendices B.7.2-B.7.3 and Figure 13.

confirmed.statement: S2 only elicits scenario selections and importance of personal style; it does not supply an additional scored writing outcome.

summary: The coding is refuted: H1a-prime belongs under diversity/across_people, and the PDF does not establish the asserted pair-level analysis units for four reference-comparison outcomes. Criterion 3 still holds because stylistic diversity is computed on participants' writing, and all retained reported numerical results match the PDF.
